chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ḥamzah ibn Ḥumrān and al-Ḥasan ibn Ziyād, they both said:

We entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام while there were people with him and he was leading them in the ʿAṣr salat, and we had already performed salat. So we counted for him in his rukūʿ: “Subḥāna Rabbiyal-ʿAẓīm” thirty-four or thirty-three times. And one of the two said in his narration: “wa bi-ḥamdih” in the rukūʿ and the sujūd. So this narration is specific to his action عليه السلام and his salat with one whom he knew could bear that, because the principle in congregational salat is lightening it, as we shall explain.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the reported authority in the narration
key_terms.التَّخْفِيفُ: making the prayer lighter or shorter for the followers
key_terms.الرِّوَايَةُ: the narration being cited and qualified
key_terms.رُكُوعِهِ: his rukūʿ, the bowing position in salat
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمِ: the tasbih recited in rukūʿ: 'Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent'

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum or normal tasbih in rukūʿ and sujūd, and may it be prolonged in congregational salat?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام prolonged the tasbih in rukūʿ during congregational ʿAṣr salat, repeating it thirty-three or thirty-four times. The concluding statement clarifies that this was specific to his practice with those able to bear it, while the general principle in congregational salat is to keep it light.
